report.summary: Users experienced 5-10 minute delays in receiving transaction SMS and push notifications starting around 14:00 UTC on 2026-10-12. Investigation revealed that the external third-party SMS vendor (sms-vendor) experienced transient latency degradation starting at 14:05 UTC, coinciding with slow outbound calls logged by notification-service starting at 14:02:53 UTC. This blocked synchronous worker threads and caused cascading message queue consumer lag in event-bus.

supporting.note: sms-vendor latency_p99_ms experienced an upward anomaly starting at 14:05 UTC, peaking at 1569.0 ms.
Consumer group notif-alerts lag recorded starting at 14:18:26+00:00 as a downstream consequence of blocked workers.

contradicting.note: push-provider metrics showed zero latency or error anomalies, yet notification-service logged a slow push call in log-00781 (7278ms), suggesting local resource contention or thread pool blocking inside notification-service.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Notification-Service Client-Side Connection Pool Exhaustion / Thread Starvation

supporting.note: notification-service had a scheduled API credential rotation configuration change on 2026-10-12 at 07:38:00+00:00.
push-provider took 7278ms in notification-service logs despite metric:push-provider:latency_p99_ms showing completely normal vendor metrics, pointing to a client-side bottleneck.

contradicting.note: chg-9140 occurred 6.5 hours prior to the onset at 14:02:53 UTC.
sms-vendor metrics independently showed an upward latency anomaly starting at 14:05 UTC on the vendor side.

supporting.note: Consumer lag anomaly started rising sharply at 14:07:00+00:00, peaking at 1006.69 messages.

contradicting.note: The first slow vendor call occurred at 14:02:53+00:00, before the event-bus consumer lag metric anomaly started rising at 14:07:00+00:00.
Event-bus CPU, error rate, and p99 latency metrics showed zero anomalies.

facts.text: push send to push-provider took 7278ms starting at 2026-10-12T14:06:19+00:00
Consumer group notif-alerts lag of 279 messages was recorded at 2026-10-12T14:18:26+00:00
notification-service depends asynchronously on event-bus and synchronously on sms-vendor and push-provider.
payments-api sends events to event-bus which is consumed by notification-service.
notification-service had a scheduled API credential rotation configuration change on 2026-10-12 at 07:38:00+00:00.
event-bus had a request timeout configuration change raised on 2026-10-12 at 05:21:00+00:00.
portfolio-service and auth-service had routine deployments shortly before the incident onset at 14:00.
sms-vendor p99 latency spiked starting at 14:05:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 1569.0 ms.
sms-vendor error rate and request rates remained stable around baseline levels during the 12:00 to 14:40 UTC window.
push-provider metrics (RPS, error rate, and p99 latency) showed no anomalies and remained entirely stable around baseline throughout the window.
The query_metrics backend for notification-service returned 503 Service Unavailable errors after 3 attempts.
Event-bus consumer lag metric anomaly started at 2026-10-12T14:07:00+00:00, rising from a baseline of ~123 messages to a peak of 1006.69 messages at 14:33:00+00:00.

assumptions: The independent p99 latency spike on sms-vendor reflects genuine vendor-side processing delays rather than purely client-side connection starvation.
evidence_gaps: query_metrics(service=notification-service) failed: query_metrics backend returned 503 Service Unavailable after 3 tries

recommended_actions.action: Coordinate with the external sms-vendor provider to investigate the root cause of their transient p99 latency spike.
recommended_actions.rationale: External vendor latency degradation directly triggered synchronous request blocking and delayed customer transaction notifications.

recommended_actions.action: Implement circuit breakers and asynchronous decoupling for synchronous vendor calls within notification-service to prevent thread pool exhaustion and queue lag buildup.
recommended_actions.rationale: External API slowdowns directly blocked worker threads and caused downstream consumer group lag on the event bus.

recommended_actions.action: Restore and verify the reliability of the notification-service metrics backend to prevent observability blind spots during future incidents.
recommended_actions.rationale: The metrics backend returned 503 errors during the incident, forcing reliance on indirect logs and external telemetry.
